streetscape.rule: Rules the generator applies per street edge, seeded by plot id + edge index; nothing here is placed item by item. Heights are above the surface the item stands on.
streetscape.pavement: Plots run to the kerb line (plot edges meet road edges; standards.roads.frontage tolerance 1 m). The pavement is the strip of each plot between the kerb face and the building line: the building line is the plot edge set back by sections[class].pavement. A plot edge on two classes takes the wider. Civic blocks keep their own 4 m walk (civic.walk, fixed by C-0) and their own objects; this standard does not dress them.

strip.status: Splice, on Aster's call, 2026-10-14: opt-in, key by key. Absent, a crossing is the single landing patch it was and no crossing list is exported, so recorded runs regenerate what they were made with. stagger: the most two landings of one crossing may stand off each other along the road. refuge: a median this wide or wider holds a refuge where the strip crosses it (starting value from UK refuge-island practice, Splice's figure from memory, Datum to confirm the source). control: the road classes whose kerb crossings carry a control (zebra: every kerb crossing, on every road class, since 2026-10-14 (lead, after Latch's rebuild: the thin edge lines of an unmarked access crossing barely read, shots/notes/note-1-crossing.png); stop and bank crossings keep the line pair); a class not listed has none. across: the crossing kinds whose strip may cross a tram track or a bay (a tram stop's crossing is the way to the platform; no kerb crossing may cross a track or a bay).
strip.why: Sky's walk of 2026-10-14, note 1: a crossing is two landings and a way between them, kerb to kerb, and the export only had single patches on one pavement (168 kerb landings, 82 without a partner across the road). A crossing is now one thing: two landings on opposite kerbs of one road and the strip across the carriageway between them (width crossings.w), a refuge where the strip crosses a median of refuge width, emitted as crossings[] in the export. A landing whose partner cannot stand (no pavement opposite, the spot taken, the way crossing a track or a bay) is not built. SF-19 keeps the sizes; SF-20 holds the rest.

Roads: the street kit is one straight street and a side street. The map graph (harbour-map.json) links the civic block to Comet Row and Sunset Way by two exit roads; nothing defines the district's road hierarchy or where those roads go.
concept: Buchanan's hierarchy: a primary ring (Sunset Way, Crown Road, Harbour Road, Comet Row) carries through traffic round the district; district distributors (the Boulevard, Market Street, Circus Road, Crown Avenue) feed it; access roads serve seven environmental areas and never link two distributors.
Every way a car can enter an environmental area is a gate. For a mission, the gates are the seal points; the Records Precinct has two.

Crown Circus is the hub (EPCOT 1966: a radial centre with transit through it). Four arms: the Boulevard south, Crown Avenue north, Circus Road west, Crown Parade (a pedestrian mall) east to the harbour.

Tram T1 runs in the Boulevard's central reservation with stops about 300 m apart. It turns on a balloon loop round the circus island (R 28), so single-ended trams need no crossover. South of Comet Row it runs on to Southside.

Sky rail S1 is the airport line (Tokyo 1964). One straight trunk: Skyport, Harbour, Crown Circus, Sphere Gardens, then the West End. It runs over public space: Circus Road's median, the circus island, the Parade and the Skyport Pier, and since brief 007 it threads the buildings over them: through the SpaceHQ drum (Crown Circus station inside), over the open Parade (the Galleries' side galleries under glazed barrel canopies, the Parade itself open to the sky; the beam on its mall pylons), through the Parade Gate block and the Skyport Tower's portal (Skyport station inside). Trains turn on a loop over the water round the skyport pad; the Skyport station stands on the pier's apron, the landside end.
The two systems cross at right angles at Crown Circus, the one interchange (sky station to tram stop ≈ 120 m).
The Records Axis: the Sphere Gardens sky station, Garden Walk, the café, the fountain, the raised table on Orbit Walk and the office door all sit on x = −160.

Players cross any road anywhere. Kerbs, medians, the tram reservation and the circus are walkable ground (no guard rails); crossings and raised tables only calm traffic. Walking distances on this sheet are measured that way: round buildings and water, straight over streets.

openQuestions.question: Is the wait for the next service the full headway, the average (half headway), or modelled from the mission clock?
openQuestions.why: The GDD says price = wait + ride from the timetable but does not define how the wait is computed.

openQuestions.question: Is there a walking pace, and does boarding count the interchange walk as part of the price?
openQuestions.why: The GDD states no walking pace; 1.4 m/s is an [S] assumption for interchange walks.

openQuestions.question: Can a boarded vehicle be seen, stopped or sealed (e.g. Alert 3 closing stations)?
openQuestions.why: The timetable assumes continuous service; the GDD travel rule does not cover closures. The plan notes police sealing stations rather than streets.

openQuestions.question: Does T2 run in both directions, and does a rider choose the shorter way round?
openQuestions.why: The GDD does not say; journeys here assume either direction on the line.
